title: TxGNN Graph Foundation Model Enables Zero-Shot Drug Repurposing Across 17,080 Diseases
whyItMatters: Published in Nature Medicine: zero-shot medical knowledge-graph foundation model ranking therapeutic indications (+49.2%) and contraindications (+35.1%) across 17,080 diseases—including rare diseases with zero approved drugs.
summary: Harvard Medical School, Stanford, and Mount Sinai researchers led by Marinka Zitnik introduced TxGNN in Nature Medicine, a graph neural network foundation model pretrained on a comprehensive medical knowledge graph spanning 17,080 clinically recognized diseases and 7,957 therapeutic candidates. Unlike prior repurposing models restricted to diseases with existing approved therapies, TxGNN performs zero-shot repurposing for neglected and rare diseases lacking any known treatment—improving indication accuracy by 49.2% and contraindication prediction by 35.1% over eight baselines while aligning strongly with real-world off-label clinician prescriptions and providing multi-hop mechanistic rationales.
technicalHighlights: Pretrained on a unified medical knowledge graph covering 17,080 diseases and 7,957 drugs to enable zero-shot drug repurposing for untreated rare diseases.
Improved zero-shot indication accuracy by 49.2% and contraindication accuracy by 35.1% over eight competing methods.
Includes an interactive multi-hop Explainer validated with clinicians, with predictions aligning closely to real-world off-label hospital prescriptions.
caveats: Computational repurposing predictions and retrospective health-system alignments still require prospective clinical trials to confirm efficacy and safety for each newly proposed indication.
institutions: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

scoreRationale.foundational: Solves zero-shot therapeutic inference across thousands of rare and neglected diseases lacking historical drug-label training data.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly empowers clinician-centered drug repurposing across over 7,000 rare diseases affecting hundreds of millions of patients worldwide.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature Medicine (2024) with rigorous zero-shot evaluation, clinician human-factors studies, and electronic health-record validation.
scoreRationale.velocity: Screens 7,957 candidates across 17,080 diseases simultaneously with transparent multi-hop mechanistic explanations.
